event: At the first shrine he sets the Slate on its pedestal; the eye lights and a deep chime sounds.
The ground splits on a shaft of blue-gold light, and a platform rises to meet him.
He rides it slowly down between carved walls whose light flows like water in channels.
The air has no temperature and no smell: nothing has lived or died or changed here.
His footsteps echo back with a precision like attention. The shrine is listening.
A tall pedestal glowing orange stands before a gate of humming blue light.
He sets the Slate on it; vibration and warmth run up his arm, and the world gains a layer.
The screen flashes: Sheikah Slate updated. Rune acquired: Magnesis.

changes.note: Link acquires the Magnesis rune in Oman Au Shrine

event: A dull iron plate on the floor glows pink, and he can feel its weight with a new sense.
He raises his hand and the plate rises, wobbling, the pull real in his arms and core.
He moves it left and sets it down, arm shaking, and the gate of light dissolves.
Over a gap too wide to jump he lays a metal plate as a bridge, and crosses as it groans.
He drags a heavy metal door aside on hidden tracks, his shoulders burning with ghost weight.
He lifts a chest out of shallow water; inside lies a short, simply made traveler's sword.

changes.note: Link takes the Traveler's Sword from the shrine's chest

event: His grip settles on it faster and surer than on the club: his hands know swords.
He lifts a metal crate with the rune and drops it on a straw dummy, which bursts apart.
The rune is not just a key. It is a weapon he can use without touching anything.
On a raised platform sits an ancient robed figure, cross-legged, in a tall wrapped hat.
Dried skin over old bones, posed in meditation, not collapse; a presence presses on his mind.
Words without sound: your resourcefulness in this trial speaks to the promise of a hero.
The figure glows gold from the hands upward and, gently, unmakes itself into light.
A small warm sphere drifts to him and settles into the Slate.
The Slate: Oman Au Shrine, Magnesis Trial. Spirit Orb acquired, 1/4.

changes.note: Spirit Orb from Oman Au Shrine: 1/4

event: The chamber is empty stone; this had been a person, patience distilled into a gift.
Hero means nothing to him. He walks back through the rooms, and the lift carries him up.
Afternoon cloud, wind and wildflowers come back at him; his breath shows in the cooling air.
The rune stays on: a rusted sword in the dirt, a far chest, hidden rivets all glow pink.
He draws the rusty sword up out of the earth with the rune and into his hand.

changes.note: Link pulls a rusty sword from the dirt with Magnesis

event: Four weapons at his belt now: axe, bone club, the new sword and the rusty one. None permanent.
The afternoon Plateau is golden; a hawk circles on a thermal, and his body aches at it.
The first day's camp is empty and cold; by the branch's tree, two creatures root in the brush.
He draws the new sword and moves between them with a control that surprises him.
One swings its club; he steps inside the arc, strikes twice, and it dissolves into smoke.
The other throws a rock; he sidesteps without thinking and puts it down with one strike.
Prying a stone from a wall, the bone club splits along its grain and falls into the grass.

changes.note: The Boko Club breaks prying a stone loose
Its broken pieces lie in the grass

event: Everything here has a shelf life. He is learning to stop being surprised by it.
Between the two shrine glows he builds a fire and roasts an apple as the old man showed him.
He eats it slowly in the grass, and for a few minutes the Plateau is just a place to sit.
Over the treeline the Abbey's dome sits like a stone, and his body remembers the beam.
The second shrine is on the hill above the Abbey; he will have to walk past the machine.
The apple core goes into the fire; he gathers his weapons and walks toward the glow.
The second shrine is the same: pedestal, chime, descent into clean, scentless stillness.
This transfer is not a new sense but force: his hands feel heavy with potential.
The Slate: rune acquired, Remote Bomb. Round or cube.

changes.note: Link acquires the Remote Bomb rune in Ja Baij Shrine

event: A melon-sized sphere of blue light forms in his palm, fizzing; set down, it rolls.
He switches to a cube: the same weight and fizz, but it stays where he puts it.
He sets a cube at a cracked wall, backs off ten paces, and blows the wall apart.
He blasts the rubble off a balanced slab; it tips, and he rides it up.
He rolls a round bomb beside a stone ball and blasts it across a gap onto a pressure plate.
Then the final chamber opens, and the joy stops.
A small, low machine on jointed legs rises, one clear blue eye, and draws a glowing blade.
It attacks in patterns, two swings and a pause; he steps back twice and strikes.
It swings again and he is late: the blade cuts deep into his forearm.
The Slate chimes: damage received, hearts 2/3. A full heart gone from one hit.

changes.note: The Guardian Scout's blade costs a full heart: hearts 2/3

event: The cut bleeds through his sleeve; the chamber smells of ozone and hot metal.
His body engages fully; he steps inside the pause and strikes three times at the seams.
He drops a round bomb, steps back, and sets it off as the machine walks over it.
The blast throws it off its legs, and he strikes again and again until it stops trying.
Its eye dims and its blade clatters free: blue-white Sheikah metal, the lightest he has held.

changes.note: Link takes the Guardian Scout's sword

event: The first weapon that feels made for his hand, given as a reward. It will break, eventually.
The second monk sits as the first did, in the same robes and hat, ready for the same ending.
The same words, word for word: the promise of a hero.
As the monk turns to light, his head inclines unbidden: not prayer, an acknowledgment.
The Slate: Ja Baij Shrine, Bomb Trial. Spirit Orb acquired, 2/4.

changes.note: Spirit Orb from Ja Baij Shrine: 2/4

event: Two orbs, two people dissolved to give them: the first gifts he carries given wanting nothing.
The old man said four; two more monks wait in shrines he has not found.
The lift carries him up into a late-afternoon sky streaked with orange and pink.
The light is the colour of warm metal; birds call tentatively, as they always do near the Abbey.
East, two or three hundred paces off, the machine sits with its eye dark, like a stone.
He has a real sword now, twenty attack, and bombs, Magnesis, and two Spirit Orbs.
Could he fight it? Stone never scratched it, and the sword would break in fifteen hits.
Not yet. But two days ago it was terror, and now it is a problem he can measure.
The monks waited ten thousand years. He can wait a few more days.
He walks to the old man's campfire, where smoke rises against the darkening sky.
The old man adds a log and hands him food without a word; the silence is comfortable now.
Four shrines, evenly spaced, one guide, one sealed edge: a curriculum built for one student.
Two down. Two to go.
